status_detail: City of Batavia says the City Council approved a master service agreement with Batavia DC Corp., a Hut 8 subsidiary, on July 21, 2025 for a proposed data center at 1780 Hubbard Ave.; secondary reports describe a 120,000 sq ft facility with capped power up to 50 MW and water capped at 1,000 gallons/day.
notes: Official city project page confirms agreement and site; capacity/status details supplemented by local/secondary sources. Likely planned/permit-approved rather than operational.

aliases: Kenyon Road and IL Route 25 data center
status_detail: A Dallas-based developer reportedly seeks to build a 200,000 sq ft data center on about nine acres at the northwest corner of Kenyon Road and Illinois Route 25 and submitted a 48 MW power request to ComEd; annexation to South Elgin was reported as part of the proposal.
notes: No county approval found in quick search; early-stage proposal identified from local/industry news.

status_detail: Village of Essex posted a development-standards and mitigation-response notice for a proposed data center facility that may be located in the village. Local reporting says Constellation bought several hundred acres in/near Essex, is seeking annexation near Braidwood Clean Energy Center, and says it has no customer yet.
notes: Very early and not a formal project application; included because village official notice explicitly references a proposed data center facility and mitigation requirements.

status_detail: Yorkville official PUD amendment page identifies an approved CyrusOne data center campus north of Faxon Road and east of Eldamain Road; revised January 28, 2026 request eliminated Building 7 and reduced total building area from 2,451,200 sq ft to 2,163,800 sq ft. DCD reported Yorkville City Council approval in July 2024 for a roughly 228-230 acre campus with up to nine two-story buildings and onsite substation.
notes: Official city page confirms approved PUD and 2026 amendment; capacity not found in official source.

status_detail: Savion, developer of the 250 MW Plano Skies Energy Center in Kendall County, is seeking to add a data center campus as part of the solar development; proposal drew local official backlash over lack of detail.

project_name: T5 @ Chicago IV Grayslake Data Center Campus
status_detail: Village of Grayslake official page says a data center campus has been approved near Peterson Road after Plan Commission and Village Board meetings. T5 announced a 480 MW Grayslake campus, already zoned for data center use, targeting first 60 MW in Q4 2027; local reporting describes a 400-acre-plus/10 million sq ft-plus campus under construction/approved with up to 1.2 GW leasable power discussed.
notes: County board member says project is within Grayslake village limits and not Lake County-approved; county separately pursued temporary deferral for unincorporated data center applications.
